newsitem.title: USA: Yamaichi N.Y. chief econ, fixed income head resign. [CORRECTED 21:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Yamaichi N.Y. chief econ, fixed income head resign. [CORRECTED 21:00 GMT]

text.p: Two top members of Yamaichi International (America) Inc's fixed income team announced their resignations in New York on Monday.

With Yamaichi having recently cut its fixed income staff in recent months, Michael Strauss, chief economist, and Patrick Lynch, executive vice president and manager of fixed income, decided to leave, Strauss said.
Lynch's resignation was effective immediately, while Strauss said he will stay on until the end of the month.
Yamaichi International (America) is a unit of Tokyo's Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd.

Strauss said that while they haven't found new jobs yet, they are separately talking to a number of firms, but that it is possible they may work together. The two had previously worked together at UBS Securities LLC before both jumping to Yamaichi a few years ago.
He said that there will no longer be an economic research department in New York.
Strauss told Reuters that he hopes to land work soon and that he plans to spend some time with his family until then.
(Corrects to delete reference to Strauss not expecting to land something for "a couple of months".)
The resignations follow a "mid-year budget review" that involved some changes in the fixed income department, said David Sexton, vice chairman at Yamaichi.
"It wasn't a (major) reduction in the labor force as it was us looking at what we were doing," he added.

Over the past month Yamaichi's fixed income department has been cut a bit. Sexton said a few have either left or been reassigned to other departments. He confirmed that there won't be a traditional economic research department with a chief economist, meaning that Strauss won't be replaced.
Sexton said they will use research resources from Tokyo and London as well as internal New York staff.

As for Lynch's position, Sexton said he won't be replaced either. Nelson Thomson, the current head trader, will take on much of Lynch's trading manager duties, while Sexton said he also will spend more time on the trading floor in a managerial capacity.

"In connection with the budget, we did not make any decisions to go out of any general areas," he said. "We've adjusted some strategies, but we're still a primary dealer. We plan to stay in the fixed income business."
